title: The Rope Crossing
logline: At a hand-pulled ferry, a passenger takes hold of a rope tied to a tree on the far bank and crosses under their own weight. Nothing of the near bank goes with them, and yet without the near bank they could never have crossed.
human_question: When something continues, what exactly is it that continues?

premise.story: A working day at a rope- or chain-pulled river or lagoon crossing: the ferryman's routine, the people and goods who depend on it, and the small talk of a crossing repeated hundreds of times.
premise.place: A rural river or lagoon crossing where a hand-pulled ferry or rope crossing still operates.
premise.experience: The unhurried rhythm of a crossing: rope through calloused hands, the boat's slow arc, and the exact moment each passenger stands on the far bank on their own two feet.

concept_links.why: The Pradeepika's own simile for rebirth-linking consciousness: a man crossing a stream on a rope tied to a tree on the near bank, landing by his own weight; continuity with nothing that physically travels.

No fixed traveller passes between one state and the next; the near bank does not become the far bank, yet the crossing depends entirely on it, echoing the method of identity and diversity held together.

what_camera_could_observe: The ferryman working the rope, hand over hand
Passengers and goods loading and unloading
The tree and its knot on the near bank
The boat's slow arc across the water
The moment each passenger steps off onto solid ground
what_must_be_real: Whether such a crossing still operates, the ferryman's real livelihood, and the community's real dependence on it.

possible_arc.opening: The rope taut across still water at first light.
possible_arc.turn: A full day's crossings, ordinary and repeated, in all weather.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the ferryman and passengers actually say about a crossing they have made for years.

requirements: A working rope- or hand-pulled ferry crossing still in daily use
A ferryman willing to be filmed over a working day
Passengers who genuinely depend on the crossing

suggestions.name: A rural river or lagoon crossing served by a rope- or hand-pulled ferry
suggestions.why: The Batticaloa area has historically had lagoon and river crossings served by small hand-pulled or paddled ferries where bridges have not replaced them.
suggestions.verify: Whether a rope- or hand-pulled crossing (as opposed to a motorised or bridge crossing) is still operating here must be confirmed before relying on it.

risks: Literalising the doctrine onto the ferry itself
The metaphor overpowering the ferryman's actual life and the community's real dependence on the crossing
drop_if: No such crossing can be found still operating, or it has been replaced by a bridge or motorised boat

connections.note: Both explore continuity without a fixed traveller: nothing crosses over unchanged, yet nothing arises without what came before.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
